items.reason: This concerns indefinite ASN.1 lengths causing NegativeArraySizeException in ASN1Decoder, distinct from the wrong-length JOSE input handled by issue #07.
Both identify the discarded ASN1Encoder writes that redundantly encode r and s before the return statement encodes them again.
Both identify getBouncyCastleProvider returning the default KeyStore provider instead of BouncyCastle.
Both identify default P-256 keys being used for ES384 and ES512 tests, leaving actual P-384 and P-521 signatures untested.
Both identify a self-consistency-only round-trip assertion that lacks independent signature verification or comparison with the original DER.
This concerns integerToBytes truncating oversized DER integer values. No golden issue describes this conversion defect; issue #07 concerns the length of incoming JOSE signatures.
Both identify silent selection among equal-priority crypto providers by discovery order, potentially choosing a non-FIPS provider when FIPS is intended.
